requirements.statement: Uploaded PDF invoices shall be processed asynchronously into a durable review queue containing supplier, invoice date, total and currency; proposed source evidence and explicit failure states shall support reviewer inspection.
requirements.rationale: Makes extraction inspectable and prevents incomplete or unsupported model results from silently becoming accounting records.
requirements.basis: “Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue.”

requirements.statement: Only an authorized reviewer's approval of the exact invoice result revision shall permit accounting submission; proposed revision binding shall invalidate approval after changes and record the reviewer and approved payload.
requirements.rationale: Prevents an automated or stale result from authorizing an accounting action.
requirements.basis: “A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API.”

requirements.statement: Repeated delivery and retries shall not create duplicate invoices. Proposed durable intake identity, transactional state/outbox and stable accounting operation/payload identity shall preserve this invariant; uncertain external outcomes shall pause for reconciliation unless the destination's verified idempotency contract permits safe replay.
requirements.rationale: A lost receipt can otherwise cause duplicate accounting entries; destination idempotency and reconciliation must be proven rather than assumed.
requirements.basis: “Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices.”

requirements.statement: Invoice documents and extracted data shall remain stored and processed in Australia across application, parser, model, database, object versions, sensitive logs, backups, recovery and accounting delivery. Regional service/model availability and processing policies shall remain explicitly unverified until supported by destination-specific evidence; overseas routing or fallback shall not be enabled.
requirements.rationale: Prevents an Australian application placement from concealing overseas model processing, backups, logging or accounting delivery. Availability and destination-policy evidence are still required.
requirements.basis: “Keep documents and extracted data in Australia; flag unverified service availability.” The invoice-workflow processes and stores invoices and sends approved fields to existing-accounting.

requirements.statement: The workflow shall accept PDF invoices up to 10 MB and reject oversized uploads before extraction. Capacity planning shall use approximately 500 invoices daily; peak-load and completion-time acceptance targets remain open.
requirements.rationale: Makes the stated upload boundary enforceable and records the workload without inventing a peak rate or processing deadline.
requirements.basis: “PDF invoices up to 10 MB, around 500 per day”

requirements.statement: Original invoices and extraction audit history shall be retained for 90 days. Proposed lifecycle controls shall cover primary records, object versions and recovery copies; retention-clock semantics, backup windows and deletion completion shall be documented and tested before production.
requirements.rationale: Preserves originals and extraction evidence for review while requiring lifecycle rules to address versions, backups and recovery copies.
requirements.basis: “Keep originals and extraction audit history for 90 days.”

measure.metric: Original and extraction audit retention period

requirements.statement: Proposed controls shall restrict access to invoice originals, extracted personal data and audit history to authorized staff, exclude document contents from operational logs, and clean up temporary parser data. Authorization-denial and cleanup tests shall demonstrate these boundaries before production.
requirements.rationale: Personal data can leak through document access, temporary parser files and diagnostic logging; these are proposed controls requiring implementation evidence.
requirements.basis: “they may contain personal data” and the invoice-workflow document, parser and audit responsibilities.

requirements.statement: Processing shall use durable queued jobs, stable invoice/job identities and bounded retries. Proposed fenced leases and stalled-job recovery shall prevent obsolete workers committing results. Exhausted or permanent failures shall enter durable dead-letter records with reason and attempt history; authorized recovery shall preserve identity, approval and uncertain-outcome safeguards. Acceptance shall cover worker termination, duplicate delivery, retry exhaustion and recovery without lost jobs or duplicate accounting effects.
requirements.rationale: A crashed worker or exhausted retry must leave recoverable work rather than lose an invoice or restart an unsafe accounting submission. The proposed PostgreSQL dead-letter path stays inside the composed workflow.
requirements.basis: User: “Use a durable job queue, stable invoice/job identity, bounded retries, a dead-letter/recovery path, approval checks and an idempotent outbound operation.”

requirements.statement: The accounting system shall remain an externally owned reference outside provisioning scope. An administrator shall supply its endpoint and credentials through secure destination configuration. Proposed adapter acceptance shall establish authentication, payload compatibility, durable idempotency and reconciliation before delivery is enabled; endpoint availability alone shall not establish compatibility or Australian residency.
requirements.rationale: The accounting system already exists; treating it as a provisioning target would change ownership and scope. Secure destination configuration and contract tests are necessary before enabling delivery.
requirements.basis: User: “An administrator will supply its endpoint and credentials; treat it as external, not a new system to provision.”
